item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record on 3B.2 is mostly negative. I found only limited, isolated accountability steps, while the dominant pattern was arbitrary detention, abusive prisons, repression of journalists and activists, military/intelligence impunity, and tolerance of proxy forces the state did not control well.

**Accepted Claims**
- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo** | **U.S. Department of State via ECOI** | **2024** | [source](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html)  
  The report says the government took some steps to identify, investigate, prosecute, and punish officials who committed abuses. This is the best positive evidence, but it is explicitly limited and did not change the overall pattern of abuse.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo** | **U.S. Department of State via ECOI** | **2024** | [source](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html)  
  The same report says security services held people incommunicado in unofficial facilities run by the Republican Guard, ANR, and military intelligence, and that authorities did not reliably observe arrest, detention, and due-process rules. This supports tolerance of abuse by police, intelligence, and prisons.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **DR Congo’s arrest of activists invokes déjà vu of growing repression** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-02-16** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/)  
  Amnesty says LUCHA activists were bundled into unidentified cars by security agents, held in unknown detention, and subjected to physical violence and death threats. This is direct evidence of abuse by security services and tolerance of arbitrary detention.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **DRC: Authorities must immediately free detained journalist** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-03-08** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/)  
  Amnesty says Stanis Bujakera’s continued detention was judicial harassment meant to chill criticism, and it explicitly calls on Tshisekedi’s government to secure his release and protect media freedom. This is strong evidence of political imprisonment rather than prevention of abuse.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-09-30** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/)  
  Amnesty says the administration failed to prevent and punish sexual violence and attacks against civilians, tolerated arbitrary detention and judicial harassment, and allowed military courts to hand down more than 100 death sentences after reinstating the death penalty.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `2B.9`

- **More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN report shows** | **Reuters** | **2024-09-12** | [source](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/)  
  Reuters reports that prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people, and that more than 260 female inmates were sexually assaulted in the chaos. This is severe evidence of lethal and sexual abuse inside state custody.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **Congo lifts moratorium on death penalty, justice ministry circular shows** | **Reuters** | **2024-03-15** | [source](https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-lifts-moratorium-death-penalty-153836346.html)  
  Reuters says the government restored executions to rid the army of “traitors” and curb terrorism and banditry. That is evidence of exemplary punishment and a hardline tolerance for punitive coercion rather than protection.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **Army disarray hobbles Congo's fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say** | **Reuters** | **2024-07-17** | [source](https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/)  
  Reuters says the government relied on Wazalendo militias, the army had no control over them, and they were poorly trained and undisciplined. Tshisekedi reportedly ordered them brought in line, which is some mitigating evidence, but the key fact is that he tolerated a proxy structure with weak discipline.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `2B.5`, `2B.9`

- **Congolese president sacks military top brass in major reshuffle** | **Reuters** | **2024-12-20** | [source](https://theprint.in/world/congolese-president-sacks-military-top-brass-in-major-reshuffle/2411531/)  
  Tshisekedi replaced the army chief, military intelligence head, and many senior officers. This is the strongest late-year remedial step I found, but it reads more like damage control than proof that he had prevented or ended abuses earlier in the year.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `2B.9`

- **World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024** | [source](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo)  
  HRW says government forces killed civilians during enforcement of a protest ban, while journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members continued to face repression. That supports a finding that the administration tolerated abuse by police and security forces.  
  **IDs:** `3B.2`, `3B.1`

**Search Gap**
I found no strong evidence that Tshisekedi systematically prevented abuse across police, military, intelligence, prisons, militias, or informal loyalists in 2024. The record is mostly repression and impunity, with only narrow, late, and partial accountability measures.
